name: Lakeway
title: Window Cleaning in Lakeway, TX | Pure Water | CleanzATX
description: Window cleaning across Lakeway, from Old Lakeway to Rough Hollow and Serene Hills. Pure water, no spots, $10 per window, a typical home about $350.
intro: Lakeway is where CleanzATX started and where most of our route days still begin. From the 1960s streets around the Live Oak course to the newest phases of Rough Hollow, we clean windows, screens and tracks on homes along RM 620, Lohmans Crossing and Lakeway Blvd.

paragraphs: Lakeway runs along the south shore of Lake Travis between RM 620 and the water, and this page covers all of it: the City of Lakeway proper plus the 78734 and 78738 addresses that share its roads. Old Lakeway is the original plat, the numbered sections around Lakeway Marina, the Live Oak golf course and Clubhouse Dr. Rough Hollow fills the south side with more than twenty sections of stucco and stone homes above three miles of shoreline. Serene Hills sits on 456 acres off Serene Hills Dr with most of its land left as preserve. Lakeway Highlands and Flintrock Falls hold the newer custom builds toward The Hills, and Bella Montagna is the gated acre lot pocket that straddles the Austin city line.

Between those big names are dozens of smaller subdivisions we work just as often. Cardinal Hills and Cardinal Hills Estates sit off RM 620 toward Hudson Bend. The Ridge at Alta Vista and Alta Vista wrap around Lohmans Crossing. North Lakeway Village and the Preserve at Lakeway cover the north side, and Lohmans Crossing Estates, Round Mountain and Tuscan Village cluster near Lakeway Regional. Every one of them has its own page in the grid below this section, with notes on the homes, the glass and the access. If your street is inside the city limits or carries a Lakeway mailing address, it is on our regular route, and the odds are good we have already cleaned a house on it.

Lakeway glass gets hit from several directions at once. Cedar pollen rolls through from December to February and live oak pollen follows in March and April, leaving a yellow film that rain only smears. The mature live oaks in Old Lakeway drop leaf litter into tracks and give spiders a roof to work under, so screens fill with webs by midsummer. On the newer side of town, Rough Hollow and Lakeway Highlands are still building, and construction dust settles on every pane downwind of a job site. Lakefront homes on the Hurst Creek arm and the main basin get lake spray on the water side and sprinkler overspray on the street side, and both leave white mineral spots that start to etch if they sit through a summer.

West and southwest facing glass is the giveaway in this town. Most view homes are built to look at the lake and the sunset, so the biggest panes face straight into the afternoon sun, and that light shows every streak, every trace of soap residue and every hard water ring. That is why we clean with pure water instead of soap. Our dual RO, four stage system with a DI resin tank brings the water to near 0 TDS, so it dries clear with nothing left behind. For spots that have already set in, hard water removal is $10 per pane, and most Lakeway homes only need it on a handful of windows, usually the ones closest to a sprinkler head.

Because we are based here, Lakeway is the anchor of our schedule rather than a trip. We group jobs by neighborhood so one truck can work a street in Rough Hollow or Old Lakeway back to back, and that density is what lets us keep prices where they are. Lead time is usually within two weeks. Gated sections like Bella Montagna, the Ridge at Alta Vista and the Peninsula at Rough Hollow need a gate code or a call box name the morning of the visit. Water fed poles reach three stories from the ground, so nothing leans on your stucco, stone or gutters, and all we need is a working hose bib and a clear path around the house. Interiors are done by hand with squeegees, drop cloths down, covered ladders for the stairwell glass.

A typical Lakeway home runs 2,500 to 4,300 sq ft, so exterior window cleaning lands between about $250 and $430, and most jobs come in near $350. At 45 to 60 minutes per 1,000 sq ft, a 3,500 sq ft home takes roughly three hours outside; add interiors at about 30 minutes per 1,000 sq ft if you want both sides done the same visit. Screens are $5 each and tracks $5 per window. Window cleaning pairs well here with gutter cleaning in the fall, when the oaks have dropped, and a driveway or patio wash in spring once the pollen is gone. Quotes go out by text, usually within the hour during business hours.

faq.q: How much does window cleaning cost in Lakeway?
faq.a: Exterior windows are $10 per window or about $0.10 per sq ft of home, with a $200 minimum. Inside and out is $15 per window. A typical Lakeway home comes in around $350 outside.

faq.q: Do you cover Rough Hollow and Serene Hills, or only Old Lakeway?
faq.a: All of it. Rough Hollow, Serene Hills, Lakeway Highlands, Flintrock Falls, Old Lakeway and every smaller subdivision between them are on our regular route, and each has its own page below.

faq.q: Can you reach the high windows on a three story Lakeway home?
faq.a: Yes. Water fed poles clean exterior glass up to three stories from the ground, so no ladder touches the house. Two story interiors get covered ladders, drop cloths and hand squeegee work.

faq.q: What are the white spots on my lake side windows?
faq.a: Mineral deposits from lake spray and sprinklers. Normal cleaning will not lift them once they set. We treat them at $10 per pane, and plans at Triannual and above include up to 5 windows each visit.

faq.q: How often should Lakeway windows be cleaned?
faq.a: Three or four times a year suits most homes here: after cedar season, after oak pollen, and before the holidays. The Clean Windows Club takes 15% off Triannual and Quarterly and 20% off Every 2 Months.

faq.q: What if it rains right after you clean?
faq.a: Rain on pure water cleaned glass usually dries clean because there is no soap film to streak. If anything looks off within 7 days, text a photo and we come back free when we are nearby.
